entries.name: Xenomega
entries.what: [EchoRelay](https://github.com/Xenomega/EchoRelay), a reimplementation of Echo VR's web services and dedicated game servers. The legacy message translation in `docs/reference/legacy-translator.md` is read from its documentation.

entries.name: kfc
entries.what: Helped write a lot of EchoRelay.

entries.name: Dualgame
entries.what: [echo-symbols](https://github.com/Dualgame/echo-symbols), the recovered symbol names this repo pulls at a pinned commit for its log symbol cache, and [echovr-modkit](https://github.com/Dualgame/echovr-modkit) with its [EchoRelay fork](https://github.com/Dualgame/EchoRelay), which back invite codes and the early-quit lockout and which `docs/engine/early-quit.md` and the invite-code design (#906) draw on.

entries.name: marshmallow-mia
entries.what: The Echo VR Linux port, the [Echo VR installer](https://github.com/marshmallow-mia/Echo-VR-Installer) (PC and Quest) and [EchoVR_Launcher](https://github.com/marshmallow-mia/EchoVR_Launcher) (Windows and Linux). Reported #133 to #137, #495, #496, #511 to #513 and #719, and wrote the merged fixes #138 to #141, #500, #502, #514 to #516 and #721. Tested nevr-runtime in #nevr-runtime-testing.

entries.name: Crafter
entries.what: [Quest-EchoVR-Installer](https://github.com/Crafter-1/Quest-EchoVR-Installer), a 3D Quest installer for Echo VR built in Unity. Reported #621, the game sending a Quest 3 player back to Home at launch, with a full logcat. Tested nevr-runtime in #nevr-runtime-testing.

entries.name: Ducky
entries.what: The reverse engineer behind the Echo Combat Quest port.

entries.name: babs
entries.what: Echo Frenzy, a community game mode for Echo VR that paved the way for others making game modes; the pipeline for editing Echo's in-game screens (Doom on Echo is built on it); EchoCraft; and the moderator tablet for kicking players from lobbies. Has been there every step of the way, before and since Echo's shutdown.

entries.name: Trodd-

notes: sprockee is listed exactly once in each rendered list: in the thanks group, in the group's ordinary order, never first. No heading, README line or project-owner text is given to the name. tools/tests/test_credits.py enforces this.

The thanks group is the six credit strings of the community installer's patcher, spelled exactly as the patcher spells them: configs/libr15.so.yaml lines 306 to 348 at 93a2a055 in the echoApkPatch repository, which is not public. The facts are recorded here and no text is copied from it.

Everyone named as having tested in #nevr-runtime-testing is also under the testers heading, whatever other heading they have. One person is one entry: Trodd- is shown with the dash under People and under Testers.
marshmallow_mia is the patcher's spelling and belongs to the thanks group only; the README shows the person once, as marshmallow-mia.
closing: Thank you to everyone in #nevr-runtime-testing, named or not.
